content: The test image shows corn stalks with dark brown/black discoloration at nodes and internodes, with straw-colored/yellowed exterior. This is clearly a stalk rot disease. Top candidates: Anthracnose stalk rot, Charcoal stalk rot, Physoderma stalk rot.

**Analysis:**

**Test image:** Two corn stalks laid on the ground showing:
- Straw/yellow colored internodes
- Dark brown/black discoloration strongly concentrated at the nodes
- The lower stalk has severe node darkening/rotting
- Cut ends expose internal tissue

**Comparison with references:**

- **Anthracnose stalk rot**: Shows shiny black external lesions, dark fibrous internal pith discoloration — somewhat similar but the black lesions tend to be more distributed along internodes, not just at nodes
- **Charcoal stalk rot**: Dry, shredded fibrous gray-brown pith with no prominent external node lesions — doesn't match
- **Physoderma stalk rot**: Shows very dark chocolate-brown/black discoloration specifically concentrated at nodes, with straw-colored internodes remaining intact — this matches the test image very closely
- **Diplodia stalk rot**: Lighter tan/brown stalk rot, less concentrated at nodes — doesn't match

The key distinguishing feature in the test image is the dark necrosis concentrated specifically at nodes while internodes remain straw-colored. This is the hallmark pattern of **Physoderma stalk rot**.
